title: Label or pixels? Why FFmpeg colors shift
fullTitle: FFmpeg Colors Shift: Is It the Label or the Pixels?

endCard.line: The full film is on the channel

scenes.narration: Pure green is two fifty five. One plain FFmpeg command later, a player shows two fifteen. Is the file wrong, or only its label? Two readers, synthetic clips.
Reader one, f f probe, prints the label. Reader two decodes the file and reads the pixels. Each first sees a case where the effect is real. Ffmpeg six point one point one.

The plain command writes no matrix tag, and the pixels are BT six oh one. Read as BT seven oh nine, green falls from two fifty five to two fifteen. Now dash colorspace bt seven oh nine alone: tagged, but the pixels are still six oh one. Off by forty.

Range works the same way. The default puts black at luma sixteen and white at two thirty five. Add dash color range p c: identical bytes on six point one, but the tag says full. A player that follows the tag shows black as sixteen.

HDR to SDR. A plain dash pix fmt puts a hundred nit white at one twenty seven, not two thirty five. Force the colorspace filter with i all, and the pixels are the same, but the tags now say bt seven oh nine.
Three commands, one pattern. Each rewrote a label over identical pixels. A wrong label can be fixed with a tag. Pixels lost cannot be.

Lost pixels look different. A red line, one pixel wide, through y u v four two zero becomes one fifty, twenty one, one forty nine. Purple. Brightness stays near eighty one. No tag brings the color back.
captions: Y stays near 81. No tag brings it back.

scenes.narration: One false alarm. Ten bit to eight bit does not band. Plain format y u v four two zero p already dithers: sixty five values, not sixty four. Only s w s dither none truncates. Six other spellings give one checksum.
For black and white, format equals gray follows the file. On a BT seven oh nine file it gives green one eighty three. The six oh one mixer gives one forty nine: thirty four levels off.

So use this: scale with out color matrix equals bt seven oh nine and out range equals t v, format y u v four two zero p, and all three tags. On a fresh card, f f probe says bt seven oh nine. Decoded, worst error one. Black sixteen, white two thirty five. The plain command is off by forty.
Check the label and the pixels together. Not tested: real footage, real players, H L G, other encoders. Test, source films and long cut: in the description.
captions: Check the label and the pixels.
